draftMethod: Original Francophone learner scenes with exact English support; Spanish-course English anchors retained as source provenance only. Independent Fable/Opus and qualified human review pending.

lessons.sourceTitleEnglish: Give the Hotel a Timeline of Lucía's Reaction
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Narrate in order what your friend ate, when symptoms began, who called for help, and what happened next.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: You are Lucía's friend, and the AI is Vicente, the duty manager: give him a clear timeline of what Lucía ate, when her symptoms began, who called 112 and what happened next, using time markers like a las 8:10, unos minutos después and en cuanto.
lessons.sourceGrammarFocusEnglish: Past narration with time markers (a las ocho y diez comió…, unos minutos después…, en cuanto llegó la ambulancia…)

sourceWordsEnglish.en: At 8:10, Lucía ate a piece of sponge cake.
A few minutes later, she started to feel an itchy throat.
As soon as I saw her lips swelling, I called 112.
The waiter brought her water and notified reception.
When the medical responders arrived, she was very dizzy.
Around 8:30, they took her to the ER by ambulance.
I don't remember the exact time, but it was before 9.
Vicente, would you like me to repeat it more slowly?

sourcePassageEnglish: At 10, at the Hotel Turia in Valencia, Vicente, the duty manager, sits down with Emma in a room next to reception.
Vicente: I need a clear timeline for the incident report about what happened to Lucía, from room 312.
Emma: At 8:10, Lucía ate a piece of sponge cake.
Vicente: Do you know if the sponge cake had any ingredient Lucía is allergic to?
Emma: Yes, the kitchen confirmed to me that it had almond flour, and Lucía is allergic to nuts.
Emma: A few minutes later, she started to feel an itchy throat.
Vicente: Did anyone on the staff help her when the symptoms began?
Emma: The waiter brought her water and notified reception.
Emma: Shortly after, she broke out in hives on her arms and started to have difficulty breathing.
Emma: As soon as I saw her lips swelling, I called 112.
Emma: The operator asked me not to leave her alone, because the swelling could get worse very quickly.
Emma: When the medical responders arrived, she was very dizzy.
Emma: The medical responders treated her right there, in the dining room, and gave her oxygen.
Emma: Around 8:30, they took her to the ER by ambulance.
Vicente: Have you had any news from the emergency department since then?
Emma: Yes, a nurse called me to tell me that Lucía was stable.
Emma: I don't remember the exact time, but it was before 9.
Emma: Vicente, would you like me to repeat it more slowly?

sourceVerbsEnglish.exampleEnglish: Lucía doesn't eat nuts because she is allergic.
Vicente starts the incident report with the breakfast time.
If someone has difficulty breathing, call 112.
The medical responders arrive at the dining room with the stretcher.

sourceGrammarExamplesEnglish: At 8:10 she ate the sponge cake, and a few minutes later she said her throat was itchy.
As soon as the ambulance arrived, the medical responders treated her in the dining room.
lessons.objectiveFrenchCourseEnglish: Distinguer les faits observés des informations rapportées et présenter une chronologie claire au responsable.
lessons.focusEnglish: Past narration with time markers and uncertainty: At 8:10; a few minutes later; I do not know the exact time.
lessons.focusFrench: Récit au passé avec repères temporels et incertitude : à huit heures dix ; quelques minutes plus tard ; je ne connais pas l’heure exacte.
lessons.teachingNotesEnglish: This is factual reporting language practice, not diagnosis or emergency-care instruction. The friend is already with qualified responders.

words.en: At 8:10, Léa ate a piece of cake.
words.fr: À huit heures dix, Léa a mangé un morceau de gâteau.

words.en: A few minutes later, she said she felt unwell.
words.fr: Quelques minutes plus tard, elle a dit qu’elle se sentait mal.

words.en: I called for help when her condition changed.
words.fr: J’ai appelé les secours quand son état a changé.
Le serveur a prévenu la réception.

words.en: The responders arrived after the call.
words.fr: Les secours sont arrivés après l’appel.

words.en: I did not see the preparation.
words.fr: Je n’ai pas vu la préparation.

words.en: I do not remember the exact time.
words.fr: Je ne me souviens pas de l’heure exacte.

words.en: Would you like me to repeat the sequence?
words.fr: Voulez-vous que je répète la chronologie ?

english: At a hotel in Montréal, Emma meets the duty manager after her friend Léa has gone with medical responders.
The manager asks Emma to describe only what she knows firsthand.
Emma says that at eight ten, Léa ate a piece of cake at breakfast.
She did not see how the cake was prepared.
A few minutes later, Léa said she felt unwell.
Emma noticed that Léa stopped eating and asked for help.
The waiter informed reception while Emma stayed with her friend.
Emma says that she called for help when Léa’s condition changed.
The manager writes down the order of events without guessing a cause.
He asks whether Emma knows the exact time of the call.
Emma says she does not remember the minute, but it was after the waiter went to reception.
The medical responders arrived and spoke with Léa.
Emma does not describe any treatment because she did not see all of it.
She knows only that Léa left with the responders.
The manager asks about the cake’s ingredients.
Emma says she cannot verify them and asks him to check the current records with the kitchen.
He reads the timeline back so Emma can correct any mistake.
Emma corrects one time estimate and confirms the facts she witnessed.
french: Dans un hôtel à Montréal, Emma rencontre le responsable de service après le départ de son amie Léa avec les secours médicaux.
Le responsable demande à Emma de décrire uniquement ce qu’elle sait de première main.
Emma dit qu’à huit heures dix, Léa a mangé un morceau de gâteau au petit-déjeuner.
Elle n’a pas vu comment le gâteau a été préparé.
Quelques minutes plus tard, Léa a dit qu’elle se sentait mal.
Emma a remarqué que Léa avait cessé de manger et demandé de l’aide.
Le serveur a prévenu la réception pendant qu’Emma restait auprès de son amie.
Emma dit qu’elle a appelé les secours quand l’état de Léa a changé.
Le responsable note l’ordre des événements sans deviner la cause.
Il demande à Emma si elle connaît l’heure exacte de l’appel.
Emma dit qu’elle ne se souvient pas de la minute, mais que c’était après le départ du serveur vers la réception.
Les secours médicaux sont arrivés et ont parlé avec Léa.
Emma ne décrit aucun soin, car elle n’a pas tout vu.
Elle sait seulement que Léa est partie avec les secours.
Le responsable pose une question sur les ingrédients du gâteau.
Emma dit qu’elle ne peut pas les vérifier et lui demande de consulter les documents actuels auprès de la cuisine.
Il relit la chronologie pour qu’Emma puisse corriger toute erreur.
Emma corrige une estimation horaire et confirme les faits dont elle a été témoin.

verbs.exampleEnglish: Léa ate a piece of cake at breakfast.
verbs.exampleFrench: Léa a mangé un morceau de gâteau au petit-déjeuner.

verbs.exampleEnglish: The manager began the report with the breakfast time.
verbs.exampleFrench: Le responsable a commencé le rapport par l’heure du petit-déjeuner.

verbs.exampleEnglish: Emma called for help when her friend’s condition changed.
verbs.exampleFrench: Emma a appelé les secours quand l’état de son amie a changé.

verbs.exampleEnglish: The responders arrived after the call.
verbs.exampleFrench: Les secours sont arrivés après l’appel.
Le serveur a prévenu la réception.

grammarExamples.english: At eight ten she ate cake; a few minutes later she said she felt unwell.
grammarExamples.french: À huit heures dix, elle a mangé du gâteau ; quelques minutes plus tard, elle a dit qu’elle se sentait mal.

grammarExamples.english: I do not know the exact time, but the responders arrived after the call.
grammarExamples.french: Je ne connais pas l’heure exacte, mais les secours sont arrivés après l’appel.

lessons.speakingInstructionEnglish: Tell the duty manager the sequence of events. Separate what you observed from what you do not know; do not infer a cause or describe treatment you did not witness.
lessons.speakingFrench: À huit heures dix, Léa a mangé du gâteau. Quelques minutes plus tard, elle a dit qu’elle se sentait mal. Je n’ai pas vu la préparation et je ne connais pas l’heure exacte de l’appel.
lessons.regionalNotesEnglish: Québec emergency and hotel reporting practices need qualified local review. No emergency number, diagnosis, treatment, or food-safety conclusion is taught.

lessons.sourceTitleEnglish: Talk Through the Mislabeled Gluten-Free Bread
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Describe a near miss calmly, without blame, and agree with the baker on what will prevent it next time.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: You are Priya's friend, and the AI is Itzel, the baker: calmly explain the misplaced sin gluten sign without blaming her, using por poco, casi and si no hubiera…, podría haber…, then agree with her on one or two steps to prevent it next time.
lessons.sourceGrammarFocusEnglish: Casi, por poco, podría haber; si clauses (por poco se lo come; si no hubiera leído la etiqueta, podría haber pasado algo)

sourceWordsEnglish.en: Excuse me, Itzel, the gluten-free sign is on another tray.
Priya, don't eat it yet; wait a sec for me.
She almost ate it, but I read the label first.
If I hadn't seen it, she could have gotten sick.
Don't worry, Itzel, nobody is to blame.
Something almost happened, but we caught it in time.
What do you think about using a color code for the trays?
Could you keep the gluten-free bread in a separate area?

sourcePassageEnglish: One Saturday morning, Daniel and his friend Priya walk into Itzel's bakery in Coyoacán to have breakfast.
Priya is celiac, so she always looks for the gluten-free bread before ordering.
Priya takes a concha from the tray that has the gluten-free sign.
Daniel reads the bread's label and sees that the ingredient list includes wheat flour.
Daniel: Priya, don't eat it yet; wait a sec for me.
Daniel: Excuse me, Itzel, the gluten-free sign is on another tray.
Itzel checks the trays and turns red, because the gluten-free bread is on the tray next to it, without a sign.
Itzel: How embarrassing, it was my oversight!
Daniel: She almost ate it, but I read the label first.
Daniel: If I hadn't seen it, she could have gotten sick.
Daniel calmly explains that, because of celiac disease, Priya can't eat anything with wheat flour.
Daniel: Don't worry, Itzel, nobody is to blame.
Daniel: Something almost happened, but we caught it in time.
Itzel says the mix-up started when she moved the trays to bring out the new batch.
Itzel: It was a scare for everyone, and we need a preventive measure so it doesn't happen again.
Daniel: What do you think about using a color code for the trays?
Daniel: Could you keep the gluten-free bread in a separate area?
Itzel: Those sound like good ideas, so starting tomorrow the gluten-free trays will be green and will be in a separate area.

sourceVerbsEnglish.exampleEnglish: Priya doesn't eat bread with wheat flour.
What do you think about using a color code?

sourceVerbsEnglish.meaningEnglish: to leave, to keep (in a place)
sourceVerbsEnglish.exampleEnglish: We keep the gluten-free bread in a separate area.

sourceGrammarExamplesEnglish: She almost ate the wheat-flour bread.
If I hadn't read the label, something serious could have happened.
lessons.objectiveFrenchCourseEnglish: Décrire une erreur d’étiquetage sans accusation, puis demander des vérifications avant toute autre vente.
lessons.focusEnglish: Near-miss and conditional language: she almost bought it; if I had not read the label, I might have missed the discrepancy.
lessons.focusFrench: Presque et conditionnel passé : elle a failli l’acheter ; si je n’avais pas lu l’étiquette, je n’aurais peut-être pas vu l’erreur.
lessons.teachingNotesEnglish: Do not present label location, color codes or separate trays as proof of gluten-free safety. The learner declines the item while staff verify ingredients and preparation.

words.en: The gluten-free sign appears to be beside the wrong tray.
words.fr: L’écriteau sans gluten semble être à côté du mauvais plateau.

words.en: Please wait before buying that bread.
words.fr: Attendez avant d’acheter ce pain, s’il vous plaît.

words.en: She almost bought it, but we read the label first.
words.fr: Elle a failli l’acheter, mais nous avons d’abord lu l’étiquette.
L’étiquette indique de la farine de blé.

words.en: We cannot verify this item from the sign alone.
words.fr: Nous ne pouvons pas vérifier ce produit à partir de l’écriteau seul.

words.en: Could you check the ingredients and preparation?
words.fr: Pourriez-vous vérifier les ingrédients et la préparation ?

words.en: Please pause the sale while you check.
words.fr: Veuillez suspendre la vente pendant votre vérification.

words.en: We will choose another option if it remains unclear.
words.fr: Nous choisirons autre chose si cela reste incertain.

english: Priya and Daniel enter a bakery in Paris for breakfast.
Priya has coeliac disease and asks about an item marked gluten-free.
Daniel notices that the sign seems to sit beside a different tray.
They read the label on the item Priya was about to buy.
The label lists wheat flour.
Daniel asks Priya to wait before buying it.
He tells the baker that the sign and the item do not match.
He does not accuse her of knowing why it happened.
The baker checks the label and moves the sign away from the tray.
She pauses sales of the affected items while she checks the batch records.
Priya says the sign alone cannot confirm whether another item is suitable.
She asks about ingredients, preparation and shared equipment.
The baker says she needs to ask the person who prepared the batch.
Daniel suggests recording how the sign became separated from its item.
The baker agrees to review the labeling steps with her team.
She does not promise that a color code or a separate tray would remove all risk.
Priya decides not to buy food until the details can be confirmed.
They thank the baker and leave with a plan to choose another option.
french: Priya et Daniel entrent dans une boulangerie à Paris pour le petit-déjeuner.
Priya a la maladie cœliaque et pose une question sur un produit portant la mention « sans gluten ».
Daniel remarque que l’écriteau semble placé à côté d’un autre plateau.
Ils lisent l’étiquette du produit que Priya allait acheter.
L’étiquette indique de la farine de blé.
Daniel demande à Priya d’attendre avant de l’acheter.
Il dit à la boulangère que l’écriteau et le produit ne correspondent pas.
Il ne l’accuse pas de savoir pourquoi cela s’est produit.
La boulangère vérifie l’étiquette et retire l’écriteau du plateau.
Elle suspend la vente des produits concernés pendant qu’elle vérifie les documents de la fournée.
Priya dit que l’écriteau seul ne peut pas confirmer si un autre produit lui convient.
Elle pose des questions sur les ingrédients, la préparation et le matériel partagé.
La boulangère dit qu’elle doit interroger la personne qui a préparé la fournée.
Daniel propose de noter comment l’écriteau s’est retrouvé séparé du produit correspondant.
La boulangère accepte de revoir les étapes d’étiquetage avec son équipe.
Elle ne promet pas qu’un code couleur ou un plateau séparé supprimerait tout risque.
Priya décide de ne pas acheter de nourriture tant que les détails ne peuvent pas être confirmés.
Ils remercient la boulangère et partent avec l’intention de choisir une autre solution.

verbs.exampleFrench: Priya a failli acheter le produit.

verbs.exampleEnglish: Daniel read the label before the sale.
verbs.exampleFrench: Daniel a lu l’étiquette avant la vente.

verbs.exampleEnglish: The baker checked the batch records.
verbs.exampleFrench: La boulangère a vérifié les documents de la fournée.

verbs.exampleEnglish: She paused the sale of the affected items.
verbs.exampleFrench: Elle a suspendu la vente des produits concernés.

verbs.exampleEnglish: They chose another option when details remained unclear.
verbs.exampleFrench: Ils ont choisi une autre solution quand les détails sont restés incertains.

grammarExamples.english: She almost bought the item marked gluten-free.
grammarExamples.french: Elle a failli acheter le produit portant la mention « sans gluten ».

grammarExamples.english: If I had not read the label, I might not have noticed the discrepancy.
grammarExamples.french: Si je n’avais pas lu l’étiquette, je n’aurais peut-être pas remarqué l’incohérence.

lessons.speakingInstructionEnglish: Describe the label discrepancy calmly, ask staff to verify ingredients/preparation, and decline to buy if the answer remains uncertain.
lessons.speakingFrench: L’écriteau sans gluten semble être à côté du mauvais plateau. L’étiquette indique de la farine de blé. Pourriez-vous suspendre la vente et vérifier les ingrédients et la préparation ?
lessons.regionalNotesEnglish: French/EU coeliac labeling and bakery cross-contact procedures require qualified specialist review. No color code, tray separation, or label alone is a safety guarantee.

lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Follow staff instructions, relay short clear commands to other guests, and phone reception from outside.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: You are a hotel guest at breakfast, and the AI is staff member Julián, guest doña Fabiola and the receptionist: follow Julián, relay commands like ¡salgan por aquí! and ¡no usen el ascensor!, guide Fabiola out with si + present → future, and phone reception from outside.
lessons.sourceGrammarFocusEnglish: Si + present → future; short radio or phone commands (si suena otra vez, saldremos; ¡salgan por aquí!, ¡no usen el ascensor!)

sourceWordsEnglish.en: Go out this way, through the emergency exit!
Don't use the elevator, go down the stairs!
Doña Fabiola, please leave the coffee and let's go out now.
If we leave now, I'll buy you another coffee afterward.
Julián, where is the meeting point?
Hello, reception? I'm calling from room 504; we're outside now.
We're on the sidewalk, with doña Fabiola and two more guests.
If it goes off again, we'll leave immediately.

sourcePassageEnglish: During breakfast in the fifth-floor dining room of the Hotel Candelaria, in Bogotá, a toaster burns and the smoke reaches the ceiling.
The smoke detector goes off right away and the fire alarm sounds throughout the building.
Julián, the hotel's emergency team member, unplugs the toaster and keeps the fire extinguisher ready next to the buffet, as the hotel protocol says.
Julián: Go out this way, through the emergency exit!
Daniel, the guest from room 504, repeats the order for the tourists at the back table: Don't use the elevator, go down the stairs!
Doña Fabiola, an older lady, stays seated and says she wants to finish her coffee first.
Daniel: Doña Fabiola, please leave the coffee and let's go out now.
Daniel: If we leave now, I'll buy you another coffee afterward.
Doña Fabiola smiles, takes her cane and walks with Daniel toward the fire door, which Julián closes behind them.
On the stairs, Daniel asks: Julián, where is the meeting point?
Julián: It's on the sidewalk, in front of the bakery on the corner.
Once outside, Daniel calls the hotel reception on his cell phone.
The receptionist, Carolina, checks the guest list to confirm that nobody is still inside.
Daniel: Hello, reception? I'm calling from room 504; we're outside now.
Daniel: We're on the sidewalk, with doña Fabiola and two more guests.
Carolina: It isn't a false alarm, so wait at the meeting point until the firefighters check the dining room.
Carolina: If the firefighters allow it, the evacuation will end soon and you will be able to go back to your rooms.
Daniel: If it goes off again, we'll leave immediately.

sourceVerbsEnglish.exampleEnglish: Go out this way, through the emergency exit!
We go down the stairs with doña Fabiola.

sourceVerbsEnglish.meaningEnglish: to sound, to go off (an alarm)
sourceVerbsEnglish.exampleEnglish: The fire alarm sounds throughout the building.

sourceGrammarExamplesEnglish: If the alarm goes off again, we'll leave by the stairs.
Go out this way and don't use the elevator!
lessons.titleFrenchCourseEnglish: Suivre les consignes pendant une alarme
lessons.objectiveFrenchCourseEnglish: Suivre les indications du personnel, transmettre des messages courts et rendre compte depuis le lieu de rassemblement.
lessons.focusEnglish: Short instructions and conditional reporting: follow the staff; if instructions change, we will listen to the response team.
lessons.focusFrench: Consignes brèves et conditionnel : suivons le personnel ; si les consignes changent, nous écouterons les secours.
lessons.teachingNotesEnglish: Emergency scene is language practice. Use the marked route and staff/response-team directions rather than inventing universal evacuation steps or promising re-entry.

words.en: The staff member is directing us.
words.fr: Le membre du personnel nous guide.

words.en: Could you repeat the meeting point?
words.fr: Pourriez-vous répéter où se trouve le point de rassemblement ?

words.en: We are outside with two other guests.
words.fr: Nous sommes dehors avec deux autres clients.

words.en: I will report what I saw, not what caused it.
words.fr: Je décrirai ce que j’ai vu, pas la cause.

words.en: Reception, we are at the meeting point.
words.fr: Réception, nous sommes au point de rassemblement.

words.en: If instructions change, we will follow the response team.
words.fr: Si les consignes changent, nous suivrons les secours.

words.en: We will wait for authorization before returning.
words.fr: Nous attendrons l’autorisation avant de rentrer.

passage.titleFrench: Suivre les consignes pendant une alarme
english: During breakfast at a hotel in Brussels, an alarm sounds in the dining room.
Daniel sees a staff member, Jules, directing guests toward a marked exit.
Daniel does not know what caused the alarm.
Jules asks the guests to follow the indicated route.
Daniel repeats the short message to the people at the back table.
An older guest, Fabiola, asks where the group is going.
Daniel tells her that Jules is guiding them to the meeting point.
Fabiola takes her cane and follows the group.
Daniel asks Jules to repeat where the meeting point is.
Jules points to the hotel’s designated place outside.
The group follows the staff directions and reaches that place.
From outside, Daniel contacts reception.
He says that he is with Fabiola and two other guests.
The receptionist records the information for the response team.
Daniel reports that he heard the alarm but does not guess its cause.
Reception asks everyone to remain at the designated point and follow the response team’s directions.
Nobody promises when the building will reopen.
Daniel tells Fabiola they will wait for authorization before returning.
french: Pendant le petit-déjeuner dans un hôtel de Bruxelles, une alarme retentit dans la salle.
Daniel voit un membre du personnel, Jules, orienter les clients vers une sortie indiquée.
Daniel ne sait pas ce qui a déclenché l’alarme.
Jules demande aux clients de suivre l’itinéraire indiqué.
Daniel répète le message bref aux personnes de la table du fond.
Une cliente âgée, Fabiola, demande où va le groupe.
Daniel lui dit que Jules les guide vers le point de rassemblement.
Fabiola prend sa canne et suit le groupe.
Daniel demande à Jules de répéter où se trouve le point de rassemblement.
Jules montre l’endroit désigné par l’hôtel à l’extérieur.
Le groupe suit les consignes du personnel et rejoint cet endroit.
Dehors, Daniel contacte la réception.
Il dit qu’il est avec Fabiola et deux autres clients.
La personne à la réception note ces informations pour les secours.
Daniel indique qu’il a entendu l’alarme, sans deviner sa cause.
La réception demande à tous de rester au point désigné et de suivre les consignes des secours.
Personne ne promet quand le bâtiment rouvrira.
Daniel dit à Fabiola qu’ils attendront l’autorisation avant de rentrer.

verbs.exampleEnglish: Follow the marked exit indicated by staff.
verbs.exampleFrench: Suivez la sortie indiquée par le personnel.

verbs.exampleEnglish: Daniel repeated the message to the other guests.
verbs.exampleFrench: Daniel a répété le message aux autres clients.

verbs.exampleEnglish: Fabiola asked where the meeting point was.
verbs.exampleFrench: Fabiola a demandé où se trouvait le point de rassemblement.
L’alarme a retenti pendant le petit-déjeuner.
Daniel a contacté la réception depuis l’extérieur.

grammarExamples.english: If instructions change, we will follow the response team.
grammarExamples.french: Si les consignes changent, nous suivrons les secours.

grammarExamples.english: Please follow the marked route and wait for authorization.
grammarExamples.french: Veuillez suivre l’itinéraire indiqué et attendre l’autorisation.

lessons.speakingInstructionEnglish: Relay short staff instructions, confirm the meeting point, and report only what you observed from outside; wait for authorized direction.
lessons.speakingFrench: Veuillez suivre la sortie indiquée par le personnel. Pourriez-vous répéter où se trouve le point de rassemblement ? Réception, nous sommes dehors avec trois autres clients.
lessons.regionalNotesEnglish: Belgian hotel evacuation and responder instructions require qualified local fire-safety review. This scene gives no universal route, emergency number, cause or re-entry promise.
